newsitem.title: USA: Chase Industries to close Indiana facility.
newsitem.headline: Chase Industries to close Indiana facility.

text.p: Chase Industries Inc said Monday it will close the Hammond, Ind., facility of its Leavitt Tube Co Inc unit.
The company said it will move the Hammond location's steel tube manufacturing operations to Leavitt facilities in Chicago and Jackson, Miss.
"This consolidation will improve profitability and customer service," Chase president Martin Alonzo said in a written statement. "The cost of this consolidation was previously provided for."

About 40 to 50 hourly wage jobs will be affected by the Hammond plant closing, said Chase chief financial officer Michal Segraves. Some workers will be transferred to Chicago, and some will lose their jobs, Segraves said.
"It's really hard to tell, but there will be some layoffs," Segraves said. The company began negotiating with union representatives about the matter Monday morning.
Chase, which also owns Chase Brass & Copper Co, acquired Leavitt in August 1996, he said.
